title: El Salvador · Bitcoin Beach
blurb: On a later stay I took a room at the Punta El Zonte hostel, where the river meets the beach. That is Bitcoin Beach, where the phenomenon started. I woke before dawn to meditate, watched the surfers paddle out, and listened to the big round stones tumble every time a wave hit.
body:
On a later stay I took a room at the Punta El Zonte hostel, where the river meets the beach. That is Bitcoin Beach, where the phenomenon started. I woke before dawn to meditate, watched the surfers paddle out, and listened to the big round stones tumble every time a wave hit.

I painted the sunrises and the sunsets later in my Seattle studio from the photos I took there. The tropical air makes the light especially luminous, and I tried to keep that on the paper. El Salvador was a pioneer in accepting Bitcoin; this stretch of sand is as fundamental to that culture as anything I know.

These three sunsets are from my first trip to El Salvador, in 2022. I stayed at a beach resort at Atami, north of El Zonte, with cabanas on the sand and daybeds in the shade. I took a surf lesson, ate at a restaurant up on a cliff, and photographed the light as it changed over the Pacific.

I painted the three later, from my photos. They are very similar scenes, and I like seeing them side by side: the same horizon with the color shifting each time. They hang together in the gallery at tjm.art/play.
note: Shared story covers Atami #1-3, El Zonte sunrises/sunset, El Tunco. Draft in stories.md + blog #326. Waiting TJ approve for plaques.

title: Burning Man Temple 2022
blurb: I painted the Temple series from my second visit to Burning Man. I photographed it in different light: blue and pink at night when the lights shifted, daytime sun, and at the end when it burned. The Temple is a cathartic place for a lot of people.
body:
I painted the Temple series from my second visit to Burning Man. I took photos of the Temple in four different lighting conditions. At night they had it lit so the lights changed from blue to pink. In the daytime it was lit by the sun. And at the end, it was lit by itself, on fire.

That is why there are four: Blue, Pink, Daytime and Flame. It is the same structure each time, and the light changes what it feels like.

The Temple is a cathartic thing for a lot of people. They bring mementos of people they have lost and things they need to let go of, and it all burns. I wanted the paintings to hold those different hours of light, right up to the burn.

title: Bass Coast
blurb: I was at Bass Coast in Merritt, BC, with the ProVibers. We had danced all through the night, and by dawn we were at the downtempo tent, still hanging out as the sun came up. I had a couple of packs of bacon.
body:
I was at Bass Coast in Merritt, BC, with the ProVibers. We had danced all through the night, and by dawn we were at the downtempo tent, still hanging out and dancing as the sun started coming up.

I had a couple of packs of bacon with me. Everybody gathered around our living room setup, and I cooked it in batches, as much as each pan would hold. People ate it as it came out and told stories about what had happened over the night.

These sunrises are from that morning light over the festival: the end of a long night and the start of a slow, happy morning with friends. [TJ TO CONFIRM: which paintings are Bass Coast #3 and #4; archived-painting-90/22/133 membership]

title: Ukraine
blurb: I painted these for an auction at my first art show and donated the proceeds to a Ukrainian family in need. My friend Val, who is Ukrainian, knew someone who could use the money. The paintings sold together, and we sent what we raised.
body:
I painted all three Ukraine pieces for an auction at my first art show, at Studio 601 [TJ TO CONFIRM: venue name], and donated the proceeds to a Ukrainian family in need. My friend Val (Valera Volfson) played music there, along with Michaela Kingslight. Val is Ukrainian, and he knew somebody who could use the money. The paintings sold together, and we sent the money to a family in Ukraine, somewhere near the front lines, I gather. I hope it went a long way for them. A dear friend bought The Mother of Kyiv for Val.

Vision of Ukraine at Peace is a mother and a daughter staring into the distance over empty golden fields under a blue sky, like the Ukrainian flag. It's meant to say there's nothing to fear on the horizon. But you notice they're alone. There's no man in the picture. She's holding flowers, as if she's mourning the child's father, who maybe the child never even met.

The girl in the flower crown might be the same woman. Maybe these paintings tell one story. There's a Ukrainian tradition of flower crowns at a springtime festival. Perhaps she wore the crown when she was young, he had to go off to war, and now she's a mother.

The Mother of Kyiv is the statue that stands in Kyiv. Just before I painted it, they had taken the Soviet crest off the shield she holds up and replaced it with the Ukrainian trident. That was a very powerful symbol. [TJ TO CONFIRM: titles of sunflower woman / Mother of Kyiv]
note: Trio story drafted (Vision / sunflower / Mother of Kyiv). Revelation included as related; confirm with TJ.

title: Sedona
blurb: All of my Sedona paintings are from a trip I took with my dad. He had heard about the energy vortexes there, and he was interested in consciousness and energy healing. The vortexes drained me and energized him.
body:
All of my Sedona paintings are from a trip I took with my dad. He'd heard there were energy vortexes there, and he's been interested in consciousness and energy healing. Someone told me the vortexes can have opposite effects on different people: they might energize you, or they might draw energy out of you. I had the second experience, and my dad was very energized. The whole thing was beautiful and worthwhile.

Bell Rock was the first place we hiked. We went all the way around it, and I painted it from a few different angles.

As we drove into town, the first thing we saw was an aura reading place, so we got our auras read together. The woman there told us she was leading a sound bath the next day, and that she'd been an opera singer in a former career. I love sound baths, and my dad had never been to one, so we went. She had a beautiful voice, and my dad said he had an out-of-body experience and a vision of an elk spirit guide.

We also sat and meditated at the Buddhist stupa, saw the chapel high up on the rocks, and wandered Tlaquepaque, an arts village built like an old Mexican town, where we watched a band play energetic traditional Spanish music for a big crowd.
note: Shared Sedona trip story drafted. Only 2 Sedona works currently in play catalog; more may join later.

title: Bitcoin Film Festival · Warsaw
blurb: I painted these for the Bitcoin Film Festival in Warsaw in 2026 and hung them in the gallery at the entrance to the theater. Tomek, who organized the festival, suggested the Hussar wings and the Bitcoin shield on the Syrenka, the protector spirit of Warsaw. The honey badger is often called Bitcoin's mascot.
body:
I painted these for the Bitcoin Film Festival in Warsaw in 2026 and displayed them in the gallery at the entrance to the theater during the festival.

I talked with Tomek, who organized the festival, about themes that would resonate, and he suggested the Hussar wings and the Bitcoin shield on the Syrenka. The Syrenka is the protector spirit of Warsaw. Her statue sits in the rebuilt Old Town Square.

The honey badger is often called Bitcoin's mascot. We usually see it fierce, fighting snakes and lions, but I wanted to show its gentle side caring for its young. There's a strong natalist sentiment among Bitcoiners that I think goes along with low time preference: caring for the next generation and valuing life. Behind it is the Genesis block, written in clear wax on the paper before anything else went down, so the wax resists the watercolor and the lettering stays raw paper.

The film poster is a frame from the film Gavin made of my journey to becoming an artist. I'm meditating on Table Mountain in my Maasai blanket with mala beads. We sat down in total cloud, and as I sat there the clouds swirled away and revealed the sunlit bay far below.
note: Three separate stories drafted; one festival plaque is fine per Gallery group preference.

title: Family
blurb: These paintings are of the people closest to me. Grandpa Howard was a saintly man and a machine-shop teacher; I painted him and three others for his memorial. One favorite shows my mom, Ruth, and Grandpa Howard with me as an infant, the first time he met me as a baby.
body:
These paintings are of the people closest to me.

Grandpa Howard was a saintly man, a true follower of Christ. Every year he went on mission trips to Costa Rica to build schools, churches and infrastructure for the indigenous people there. He was a machine shop teacher his whole career, and I have fond memories of him in his shop, full of huge old cast-iron machines, where he taught me lots of things. I painted him, along with three others, for his memorial and gave them to his children.

One of my favorite pieces shows my mom, Ruth, and Grandpa Howard with me as an infant. I think it was the first time he met me. It hangs on my mom's wall.

My aunt Fran is a lifetime musician and one of my musical inspirations. I learned a lot from her when I was young, and we recently had an awesome jam at her home in Hotchkiss, Colorado. Her daughter Hillary is one of my art inspirations. She teaches at the Marchutz School in Aix-en-Provence, and her advice shaped a lot of how I paint. I visited her there with my sister, Chelsea, and she was the ideal guide to France.

title: Cape Town
blurb: These come from a trip to Cape Town with my friend Gavin for the Adopting Bitcoin conference. On Table Mountain the clouds blew away while I meditated and revealed the bay far below. On my last day I watched the sunset from just below the peak of Lion's Head.
body:
I went to Cape Town with my friend Gavin for the Adopting Bitcoin conference. Gavin grew up in South Africa and has a place near Lion's Head and Table Mountain. Both are gorgeous hikes.

We climbed into the clouds on Table Mountain. At the top it was socked in and the wind blew hard. I sat on an outcropping near the edge to meditate, and the clouds blew away to reveal the bay far below and the open ocean, nothing between us and Antarctica. That moment became the poster for the Coined in Watercolor film.

On my last day I raced up Lion's Head for sunset. In shoes with no grip, I stopped at the sign for the chains and watched the sun go down from just below the peak.

Later I gave a bunch of ProViber portraits away at a ProVibers reunion and accidentally included the Lion's Head sunset. A friend there had just been to Cape Town with his wife. I had painted their engagement in Austin, and he asked if he could have the South Africa sunset too, so I gave it to him.
note: Draft from stories.md dictation; ids matched by title in gallery-courtyard/data/white-border-317.json. 'Sunset on Lion's Head' was given to a friend at a ProVibers reunion (now private collection?) — confirm with TJ.

title: El Salvador · Past, Present and Future
blurb: I painted this triptych in 2022 with Chase Toole, after my first trip to El Salvador, right after the gangs were arrested. Nobody outside knew yet whether it would work out, and I wanted to show that tension. Past, Present and Future move from the bad years to a nation reborn to a new financial center.
body:
I painted these in 2022 with Chase Toole, after my first trip to El Salvador, right after Bukele arrested the gangs. The outside world wasn't sure it would work out, given the history of Latin American authoritarians, and I wanted to show that tension. It has turned out well, but at the time nobody knew.

Past shows the bad years: bandits with swords and knives coming out of the jungle to attack the state, the lion. Present shows a scary monster with a kind face and many arms, cradling an infant in a bubble as it rises from the ocean: the nation reborn, protected by a state that is scary but kind. In Future, feathered serpents chase the demons away and guard the birth of a new financial center.
